subject: POC success criteria & timeline — Aurora Analytics trial planning
body:
From: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Cho <sarah.cho@aurora-analytics.com>, Tom Reed <tom.reed@aurora-analytics.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 03 Nov 2026 15:12:00 -0800
Subject: POC success criteria & timeline — Aurora Analytics trial planning

Hi Sarah / Tom —

Great to meet earlier. This thread is a short recap + proposed POC plan so we can lock scope and owners. I captured the success metrics we discussed on the call and a recommended 3-week cadence that maps to your evaluation window.

High-level objective
- Validate Redwood inference for Aurora’s question-answer pipeline over internal docs and live QA traffic; demonstrate acceptable latency, throughput, cost, and accuracy so you can decide on Dedicated capacity.

Proposed success criteria (pass/fail checkpoints)
- Latency: p95 per-token/service latency <= 200 ms for typical 512-token requests on n1-standard workload (baseline traffic profile).
- Throughput: sustain 60 requests/sec with <= 1% error rate during a 10-minute window (simulates spike).
- Cost: average inference cost <= $0.45 per 1k tokens at configured batching/quantization for baseline prompts (we will provide cost estimate worksheets).
- Quality / accuracy: 40 prompt set A/B evals with human labels; pass rate >= 90% (binary relevance), mean human rating >= 4.2/5, and hallucination occurrences < 2% of responses.

Evaluation plan (3-week timeline)
- Week 0 (pre-work, 3 days): data access, sample prompt set delivery, and infra provisioning. Deliverable: sample payloads + Drive folder. Owner: Aurora (Sarah) + Redwood SE (Ben).
- Week 1 (integration & baseline): connect sample data, run baseline inference with host model variants, capture p50/p95 and cost. Deliverable: baseline report. Owner: Ben.
- Week 2 (optimization & tuning): test batching profiles, prefix caching, and quantized model variant; measure throughput & cost curves. Deliverable: optimized config + test results. Owner: Ben + Marcus.
- Week 3 (evaluation & handoff): run formal quality evals with human raters (Aurora) and final SLA recommendation. Deliverable: pass/fail summary and recommended deployment mode. Owner: Grace + Aurora PM.

Key open items (need by Fri Nov 6)
1) Sample prompt set (40 prompts + expected answers) — Sarah
2) Network egress/IP allowlist + preferred region (us-west) — Tom
3) Data retention/PII constraints doc — Sarah
4) Signed POC scoping doc (attached template) — Aurora legal

Next steps
- If this matches your expectations I’ll send a formal POC statement of work (SOW) using the Redwood template and we’ll schedule a 30-min kickoff for Monday Nov 9.

Thanks — looking forward to running this with you.

Best,
Grace O'Connor
Senior Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference
grace.oconnor@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0142

Attachments: aurora_poc_requirements.xlsx (worksheet), redwood_poc_template.pdf (SOW template)

Date: Wed, 04 Nov 2026 09:30:00 -0800
Subject: Re: POC success criteria & timeline — Aurora Analytics trial planning

Thanks Grace — this looks great and aligned. A few quick notes:
- We can deliver the 40 prompts by EOD Nov 6.
- We prefer US-WEST region for latency tests (closest to our prod).
- On cost target: $0.45 /1k tokens is acceptable as a stretch — can you include a roll-up showing expected costs at 10k /50k /200k tokens?

Kickoff Monday Nov 9 at 10am PT works for our team. Please send the SOW.

Cheers,
Sarah

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>, Sarah Cho <sarah.cho@aurora-analytics.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 05 Nov 2026 07:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: POC success criteria & timeline — Aurora Analytics trial planning

Quick technical note on measurement approach so everyone is aligned:
- Latency: we’ll report p50/p95 for end-to-end request (client -> Redwood -> model -> response). I’ll provide a small test harness (curl + session token) you can run from Aurora infra to validate network contribution.
- Throughput: measured at sustained RPS from our dedicated test harness; we’ll also validate with a short 10-min spike to ensure autoscaling/fallbacks.
- Cost: I’ll attach a simple calc in the Drive folder. The $0.45 target assumes using the q4_k8 quantized variant and batching of ~8. If you prefer conservative configs we’ll show both.
- Quality: we recommend 3 human raters for the 40 prompts (blind) and an automated score for exact-match & semantic-similarity to speed iteration.

I’ll upload the harness and initial run script to the Drive before the kickoff.

Ben
Senior Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com

See you Monday — Grace
